scope_note: Foundational accounts re-audited under study-modeling-policy 1.3.0 after renewed direct-evidence searches. Apple Mesa retains three narrowly scoped business-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals from its project fragment; Switch Citadel retains four exact fiscal arithmetic or break-even syntheses; Digital Crossroad Hammond retains two two-account paid-tax arithmetic or break-even syntheses from its project fragment. All other legacy foundational estimates were removed because direct inputs, project scope, time profiles, local allocation, causal identification, or decision relevance were not defensible. Reported observations, forecasts, and remaining models stay separate. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00116005354: Post-audit last-resort modeling gate for Apple Maiden. No estimate survives: campus and company/county evidence cannot be allocated to IM3 building 00116005354, annual incentive observations have unresolved municipal and service-cost gaps, contractor identities lack spend and geography, employment snapshots lack payroll and residence, and county aggregates lack a defensible treatment share or counterfactual. The direct-evidence fragment records every candidate-specific rejection and leaves unresolved metrics as gaps rather than fabricating building shares, tax receipts, utility use, multipliers or causal effects. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Last-resort NAP7 modeling pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact, same-property-account fiscal-year 2027 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed property-tax bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, resource, community and county outcome candidates were rejected because compatible NAP7 inputs or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Last-resort Markley Lowell model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. The only retained synthesis is an exact same-account FY2026 assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even identity. It uses the directly observed four-quarter real-property bill without estimating actual public cost, cash collections, recipient distributions or net fiscal impact. Investment, construction, supplier, operations, fiscal-net, resource, community and each GDP, employment and wage candidate are rejected separately in the evidence fragment because compatible inputs, scope alignment, non-overlap proof or credible identification are unavailable. prj_study_im3_building_00300974499: Corrective policy-1.3.0 synthesis. Three legacy combined real-and-personal-property FTZ counterfactuals are superseded by narrower business-personal-property-only estimates because the Apple BPP account directly exhibits the 5% assessment ratio while the real-property account has a different valuation base. The replacements hold observed effective tax rates and full cash value constant and isolate only the assessment-ratio component; they are not cash grants, audited forgone-revenue amounts or net fiscal benefits. All other legacy Apple Mesa estimates fail the direct-evidence, scope, time-profile, geography or decision-relevance gates and are marked for removal in the evidence fragment. prj_study_im3_building_00359930465: Post-fifth-pass last-resort modeling gate for Equinix Seattle SE3 retains eight bounded syntheses. Construction is represented separately by the AGC/DJC $50 million-$100 million award-category sensitivity and a 50,482-hours wage benchmark; neither is audited spend or certified payroll. Opening evidence for 24-hour operations and security supports only a conditional one-active-post coverage floor and wage-cost benchmark, not observed posts, headcount, payroll or total staffing. The 2011 lease's up-to-9-MW allocation remains a 25/50/100-percent throughput sensitivity, with separate statewide/tariff price and eGRID NWPP location-based emissions benchmarks that are not bills, measured emissions or market-based results. A medium-confidence identity sets the 2026 same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold equal to the exact landlord-parcel bill; it does not estimate actual public cost, tenant pass-through, cash receipt, recipient distribution or net fiscal impact. A supplier/non-labor residual is rejected because the award category does not define cost coverage and the reported hours do not establish complete labor coverage; community and causal county-effect candidates still fail for lack of compatible inputs or identification. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00388148510: Project-scoped modeled synthesis for TierPoint Little Rock. Eleven resolved-year real-property taxable values are multiplied by signed code 03/33 school, city, and county millage components; 2025 is excluded because its observed Amount Due does not disclose the underlying revised taxable value. A conditional zero-leave FTE-equivalent floor translates the facility-specific 2012 onsite NOC staffed 24/7/365 statement without claiming employee headcount or payroll. Two low-confidence engineering sensitivities use one, not both, of the redundant 3,000 kVA utility transformers and expose hypothetical power-factor, utilization, and PUE assumptions. Every estimate is modeled_not_observed_or_audited and excluded from sourced-record counts, cash receipts, realized-benefit totals, and net-fiscal claims. prj_study_im3_building_00397914434: Corrective last-resort modeling pass for Apple Prineville. Five narrow, unallocated syntheses now survive: a same-land-account tax-payment break-even identity; a 2018 campus/company payroll sensitivity anchored to the reported 100 jobs and three official BLS Central Oregon occupation benchmarks; FY2025 campus electricity-cost sensitivity using EIA Oregon customer-class averages after PacifiCorp direct-access tariffs proved noncomputable from public inputs; deterministic FY2025 average-load conversion; and an EPA eGRID location-based electricity-emissions factor sensitivity. None is allocated to IM3 building 00397914434. The cost range is not Apple's bill, the payroll range is not observed payroll, and the emissions range is not Apple's market-based Scope 2 result and preserves Apple's 100 percent renewable-electricity claim. Investment, construction, supplier, community, net-fiscal and causal county-outcome candidates remain rejected for missing scope-compatible inputs or identification. prj_study_im3_building_00438078069: Second corrective modeled-synthesis pass for Meta Altoona. Exact annual active-account property-tax aggregations and the 2024 equal-cost public-service threshold implement study-modeling-policy 1.3.0; deterministic average-load conversions, labor-hour equivalence, explicitly stylized payroll sensitivities, and noncausal county comparison gaps retain every input and overlap limitation. All results remain unallocated to the selected 315,400-square-foot IM3 building. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00472761713: Third-pass modeled synthesis for NYSE Group's U.S. Liquidity Center in Mahwah. Three 2025 parcel-levy allocations use certified recipient rates that reconcile exactly to the direct parcel bill; a same-account break-even identity states the public-cost decision threshold without estimating cost or net benefit. A wide 28 MW utilization sensitivity exposes the theoretical annual site-electricity scale, a four-quarter WIPP conversion preserves parcel and period limits, and a zero-leave 24x7 support-coverage equivalent remains location-unallocated. All estimates are modeled_not_observed_or_audited and excluded from direct-record totals. prj_study_im3_building_00499403180: Third corrective synthesis for Microsoft's Central Washington portfolio and unallocated MWH campus context. Source-modeled EY/IMPLAN operating and construction contribution outputs are preserved at Chelan-Douglas-Grant scope without conversion to selected-building effects. The direct-compensation proxy uses the reported 377 jobs and rounded $93,000 compensation at the same regional scope. Campus electricity savings are converted only to an average-load equivalent; QWRU water availability is converted only from cubic meters to gallons. Four complete MWH real-plus-personal tax-year totals and four equal-cost identities are retained for 2022-2025, but no actual public cost or net fiscal sign is asserted. Six county comparison gaps are low-confidence descriptive benchmarks for the separate 2007 Columbia event and 2015 MWH context, never causal effects. All estimates are unallocated to the 143,439-square-foot IM3 footprint and subject to explicit non-additivity. prj_study_im3_building_00500820007: Third corrective modeled-synthesis gate under project-worker research Contract 3.1.0 and study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Seventeen bounded syntheses survive: nine exact Winner-only annual paid-property-tax aggregations for 2017-2025, the 2025 same-scope marginal-service-cost break-even identity, one deterministic 2018 gross-before-realized-abatement counterfactual, one low-confidence 2020 operating-payroll sensitivity, three 2024 resource syntheses, and two explicitly noncausal 2024 county employment and wage comparison gaps anchored to the 2017 operating date. The electricity-cost central benchmark now uses the 2024 Texas industrial price; the 2024 commercial price is only a separate class sensitivity. The location-based emissions estimate uses ERCT alone; Texas state-output geography is excluded from the interval. The county GDP comparison is rejected because its national +11.080969% gap reverses to -3.263943% with Texas-only donors, making a single central descriptive value misleading. MMI Southwest is excluded from every Winner aggregation. None is a new source observation, selected-building allocation, audited recipient receipt, actual payroll, utility bill, peak demand, actual or market-based emissions, observed public cost, net fiscal result or facility effect. Construction, supplier, induced, county-GDP, actual-bill, market-based-emissions and net-fiscal models remain rejected. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Dedicated last-resort model-eligibility pass for State Farm Olathe under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Four bounded syntheses are retained: the exact 2025 parcel-tax-payment identity as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, plus low-confidence descriptive 2024 Johnson County GDP, employment and wage comparison gaps using the repository's pre-2016 inverse-distance benchmark. No estimate is an observed cost, net fiscal result or causal facility effect. Supplier/local-spend and community-allocation candidates, an HPIP credit counterfactual, and causal county designs are rejected because the project-specific inputs, scope matches, non-overlap proof or identification conditions recorded in the evidence fragment are absent. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00838817907: Corrective metric-specific synthesis for TierPoint Charlotte Center Park (CL4). Two independent staffing-equivalent sensitivities translate facility-specific continuous NOC and security coverage statements into the FTE capacity needed to cover one simultaneous post; neither is an observed employee count, the functions are not summed, and employer, overlap, shift, absence, residence and payroll remain unknown. A separate opening-configuration electricity sensitivity annualizes the directly reported 1.215 MW usable UPS capacity across utilization and PUE scenarios while checking the source-reported 3,000 kVA service capacity under power-factor assumptions. It is a theoretical nameplate envelope, not metered use, a true-value bound or an economic contribution. No model is created from 530 tons of cooling because electrical demand would require unobserved COP, part-load, redundancy and operating-hour inputs, and no model is created from generator counts, unit ratings, runtime or fuel storage because emergency standby nameplates do not measure annual operation. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass model review retains one bounded resource identity only. It reproduces Google-reported 2024 Montgomery County water consumption as withdrawal minus discharge after converting displayed million-gallon values to gallons, with a rounding envelope. Direct searches of Clarksville utility/public-works pages, county stormwater records, TDEC/EPA portals and CDE/TVA materials did not surface a building meter, utility bill or a compatible canonical observed-water metric. The amount remains unallocated across the location and inventory buildings; discharge may be engineering-estimated. No transferred multiplier, supplier-retention assumption, energy proxy, fiscal result, public-cost threshold, payroll estimate or causal county outcome is modeled. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits. prj_study_im3_building_00903236619: Third-pass modeled contribution review retains two low-confidence, last-resort sensitivities after direct-source exhaustion. The first converts the contractor-reported 1.4 MW whole-facility redundant available-power nameplate into annual electricity throughput at 25%, 50% and 100% utilization, with the high endpoint explicitly treated as a mathematical ceiling. It does not apply PUE because the source does not distinguish utility-input, critical IT or redundant-path capacity. The second combines the trade-reported approximately 70 electricians, the 234-day groundbreaking-to-report interval and BLS's near-period Detroit-area mean electrician wage into a 25%, 50% and 100% worker-duration wage-payroll sensitivity. It is limited to the reported electrician subset and excludes benefits, overtime, other trades and residence effects. No operating staffing, investment, supplier, community, fiscal/public-cost, emissions, water or county-effect model passes: no source requires continuous on-site coverage; the MCE $4.8 million field is undefined and postdates a site redesign; separate real and personal accounts lack bills and payments; the recovered City subsidy report omits this project; and no site-linked operating, recipient or counterfactual inputs exist. prj_study_im3_building_00978934687: Corrective residual synthesis for Digital Crossroad DX-1 under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Of 43 legacy estimates, none is retained unchanged: 41 are directed for removal and two are revised using the complete 2024-pay-2025 paid-tax base for the leasehold real account and DX Hammond JV LLC personal-property account. The revised contribution is an exact account-level aggregation across local taxing authorities, and the companion public-service-cost estimate is only the equal-cost break-even identity; neither is an audited recipient receipt, observed public cost or net fiscal result. New estimate IDs prevent silent mutation of the legacy base and their notes identify the superseded estimates for orchestrator reconciliation. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution. prj_study_im3_building_01132541700: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Residual synthesis after the Meta Prineville direct-evidence audit. One medium-confidence unit conversion carries Meta's rounded 2024 facility-level water-withdrawal observation from megaliters to gallons because the shared direct register has no compatible annual-withdrawal metric. The three low-confidence county benchmark comparisons were removed: even with fit-sensitivity envelopes and explicit non-causal labels, they do not materially improve decisions about this campus and remain vulnerable to concurrent Meta expansions, Apple's separate campus and unrelated county changes. No supplier, construction, payroll, household-spending, tax-abatement, public-service-cost or fiscal-net model is retained because local inputs and same-scope evidence are insufficient. prj_study_im3_campus_00231769626: Residual synthesis after the Google The Dalles public-source audit. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparison gaps are retained because the direct record does not identify causal county outcomes. Each benchmark uses the available 2001-2005 pre-opening history, excludes all study counties from a 20-county inverse-distance-weighted donor pool, and carries a fit-sensitivity envelope. No model converts broad investment or permit values to jobs, onsite contractor counts to supplier output, utility-system loads to campus consumption, tax bills to payments, or unmatched incentive formulas and public costs to a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_campus_00578435601: Directed fourth-pass model review retains eight bounded estimates grounded in published Douglas County or official national inputs: three presentation-preserving water-consumption conversions, one ECHO DMR-flow annualization, two county-M&O-only gross-levy counterfactuals on exempt personal property, one historical employee-threshold wage-bill sensitivity, and one permit-remodel construction-payroll sensitivity. Every estimate remains unallocated, non-audited, and outside direct-record totals. Tax counterfactuals are not bills, payments, tax avoided, realized abatement, net fiscal benefit, or all-jurisdiction liability; wage and construction results are transferred benchmarks rather than observed Google payroll; DMR flow is not consumption or utility-billed volume. Supplier retention, electricity use/cost, actual public-service cost, and causal county outcomes remain unsupported. prj_study_im3_campus_00675108684: Dedicated last-resort Boydton model-eligibility pass under study-modeling-policy-1.3.0. Retained syntheses are limited to exact arithmetic over cited compatible observations: a five-fiscal-year average of the operator-reported portfolio property-tax total, its explicitly conditional same-scope public-cost break-even identity, and annual sums of identified LVL/Herbert Fund 301 components. All remain unallocated, modeled rather than observed, and non-additive to their source totals. COF phase investment, operating headcount, construction, resources, suppliers, induced effects, causal comparisons and net fiscal impact were rejected because overlap, timing, scope or required project inputs remain unresolved.

sources.notes: Reports an AZNM subregion annual total-output emission rate of 706.189 pounds CO2e per MWh. The rate supports a location-based gross-emissions benchmark, not Apple's market-based inventory.

sources.title: Apple Environmental Progress Report 2025
sources.notes: Reports that a pilot resin-treatment system reduced makeup-water use by 30 percent and was being implemented at Mesa. It does not report completion, Mesa applicability, or measured Mesa savings.

sources.title: Avoiding Waste Heat through AI Infrastructure Thermal Integration
sources.notes: Reports an industry-average data-center PUE of approximately 1.4 in 2023. The value is used only as a conservative sensitivity bound, not as a Tahoe Reno 1 observation.

sources.title: Tesla Expansion Economic Impact Analysis
sources.publisher: Nevada Governor's Office of Economic Development
sources.notes: Public same-region IMPLAN analysis reports $1.6 billion of direct industrial-construction spending, 9,275 direct person-year jobs, and $924.023 million of direct labor income for 2023-2027 in Washoe and Storey Counties. Its asset mix, scale, timing and contractor mix differ from Citadel; the transfer is therefore sensitivity-tested and used only for direct construction channels. The report combines indirect and induced channels, so those channels are not transferred.

sources.title: Nevada Data Center Abatements
sources.publisher: Nevada Governor's Office of Economic Development
sources.notes: Current public program summary states that data-center applicants must ensure at least 50% of construction workers are Nevada residents. This is a compliance threshold, not an observation of Switch worker residence, hours, payroll or supplier location.

sources.title: Switch February 2019 Investor Presentation
sources.publisher: Switch, Inc. / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
sources.notes: The filed presentation reports Tahoe Reno 1 opened in 2016, 1.36 million gross square feet, up to 130 MW delivered power at full build-out, 30% utilization by available data-center space and 58% utilization by available cabinets/power capacity for the 2018 operating snapshot. Capacity and utilization are not meter readings.

sources.title: Tahoe Reno 02 Citadel Campus One-Sheet
sources.notes: Operator marketing reports 100% renewable campus power, more than 3,300 acre-feet of effluent-water availability, and 1.18 PUE for one sector. The PUE is a benchmark bound only; it is not a Tahoe Reno 1 whole-building annual measurement. Water availability is not consumption.

sources.title: eGRID2023 Summary Tables, Nevada State Output Emission Rate
sources.notes: eGRID2023 reports a Nevada total-output rate of 642.7 lb CO2e/MWh. The statewide 2023 generation-average factor is used for a location-based scenario and does not measure Citadel's supplier, contract instruments, hourly marginal emissions or market-based Scope 2 result.

sources.title: BLS QCEW annual averages, Storey County total covered employment, 2011-2019
sources.notes: Study panel values use annual QCEW total covered employment for Storey County (FIPS 32029): 3,090, 3,424, 3,893 and 4,797 in 2011-2014; 11,105, 17,199 and 17,997 in 2017-2019. The series covers all employers and is strongly confounded by Tesla and broader Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center growth.

sources.title: Prince William County Data Center Market Study
sources.notes: Tables 7 and 8 report direct, indirect, induced and total construction and operating employment, labor income and output for a county prototype using IMPLAN. Dollar values are 2021 dollars; the underlying IMPLAN data vintage is not disclosed.

sources.title: Northwest Indiana Economic Recovery and Resilience Plan
sources.notes: Reports that roughly 117,000, or about 55 percent, of resident workers also work in Lake County. This is a regional workforce benchmark, not project worker-residence evidence.

These values are not Hammond measurements.

sources.title: eGRID2023 Summary Tables, Revision 2

sources.title: Direct Access
sources.notes: Oregon PUC explains that a direct-access customer's local provider supplies distribution while a certified electricity service supplier supplies generation and transmission. The page establishes why a public utility tariff alone cannot reveal Apple's total energy cost.

Schedule 748 shows that direct-access delivery billing varies by delivery voltage, basic and facilities charges, facility capacity, on-peak demand, reactive power, Schedule 90 adjustments, metering and contract conditions; it does not disclose Apple's ESS energy price.

Together with Schedules 294-296, it confirms that transition treatment depends on direct-access election type, enrollment vintage, voltage and time period; Apple's election and enrollment vintage are not public.

sources.title: eGRID2023 Summary Tables, Revision 2
sources.notes: EPA reports total-output CO2e rates of 635.267 lb/MWh for the NWPP/WECC Northwest subregion and 365.0 lb/MWh for Oregon state generation. The model treats these as geographic-factor sensitivity anchors, not Apple's contractual or market-based emissions.

sources.title: Meta 2025 Environmental Data Index

sources.title: Electric Power Annual 2024 — Table 2.10, average electricity price by state and sector
sources.notes: Final EIA-861 table reports Texas average retail electricity prices of 6.12 cents/kWh industrial and 8.55 cents/kWh commercial for 2024, and 6.60 cents/kWh industrial for 2023. sources.title: Oncor Tariff for Retail Delivery Service
sources.notes: The current PUCT-approved delivery tariff lists Tarrant County in Oncor's certified service area and shows distinct primary-distribution, primary-substation and transmission-service schedules with customer, metering, demand and rider charges. It establishes why kWh alone cannot reconstruct Meta's historical delivery or total bill; the current tariff is not used as a 2024 price.

sources.title: Texas Public Utility Regulatory Act — customer choice, metering and billing provisions
sources.notes: PURA separates the retail electric provider from the transmission and distribution utility in customer-choice areas and provides that the utility bills nonbypassable delivery charges to the retail provider. Meta's provider, contract price, rate class and meter determinants are not public, preventing an actual-bill estimate.

estimates.label: SE3 lease-capacity annual electricity-throughput sensitivity

period.label: Annualized engineering sensitivity from the executed lease's prospective 9 MW allocation

scope.label: Equinix SE3 leased premises at 2020 Fifth Avenue; no customer, cabinet or meter allocation

interval.interpretation: The lease's up-to-9-MW allocation is annualized at 25%, 50% and 100% utilization. The high endpoint is the mathematical continuous-load ceiling for that contractual allocation, not a forecast, true-value bound or confidence interval.

parameters.name: lease_power_allocation

provenance.detail: Executed lease allocation from two Seattle City Light vaults, limited to 4.5 MW actual draw from either vault

parameters.transformation: Converted to kW and multiplied by annual hours and utilization

provenance.detail: Non-leap-year annualization
Low order-of-magnitude throughput scenario
Central order-of-magnitude throughput scenario
Continuous full-allocation mathematical ceiling

estimates.confidence_rationale: The lease allocation is project specific, but it was prospective, and no public record verifies commissioning, current availability, meter boundary or utilization. The 9 MW may describe utility allocation rather than IT load.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides an explicit order-of-magnitude throughput sensitivity and contractual ceiling without relabeling allocated capacity as consumption. Separate models apply external price and grid-emissions factors without changing this model into a bill or emissions observation.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Commissioning record, current utility entitlement, interval meter data, bills, peak demand, occupied IT load, site PUE, customer allocation, electricity price, renewable share and emissions

derivation.formula: 9 MW × 1,000 kW/MW × 8,760 hours × allocation-utilization scenario
assumptions: The up-to-9-MW lease allocation is used once; the two 4.5 MW vault limits are not added again.
Utilization scenarios are 25%, 50% and 100% solely for sensitivity.
No PUE multiplier is applied because the lease describes tenant electrical allocation and publishes no IT/facility boundary.
The result remains at the SE3 leasehold level and is not allocated by colocation square footage, cabinet count, customer occupancy or assessor area.

limitations: No meter reading, utility bill, observed load factor or commissioning record.
The 2011 prospective allocation may not equal current available, critical IT or occupied load.
The interval is a scenario range, not a statistical or empirical physical bound below the stated ceiling.
This model alone does not infer electricity cost, emissions, revenue, output or fiscal effect.
estimates.notes: Resource sensitivity only. The direct up-to-9-MW source projection remains authoritative; this model is neither observed consumption nor an economic contribution and must not be added to monetary records.

provenance.detail: AGC/DJC project profile total worker hours

High sensitivity for a skilled-trade and overtime mix above the metropolitan major-group mean

estimates.label: Zero-leave minimum continuous-coverage FTE-equivalent

period.label: Conditional annual coverage equivalent from the 2012 onsite NOC staffing statement

scope.label: At least one continuously occupied onsite NOC coverage position at the Windstream/TierPoint Little Rock data center; employment relationship unallocated

interval.interpretation: Mathematical zero-leave lower bound conditional on the facility-specific statement that the onsite NOC was staffed 24/7/365; not observed employee headcount.

provenance.detail: Facility-specific statement that the onsite network operations center was staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year
Forty scheduled hours per week for 52 weeks, with zero leave, training, breaks, overlap, or relief allowance

estimates.confidence_rationale: The continuous onsite staffing statement is facility-specific and the division is exact. The result is conditional and cannot distinguish employees from contractors, actual headcount, multiple simultaneous posts, leave relief, residence, occupation, or payroll.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a conservative floor for the labor coverage embodied by a documented 24x7 onsite operating function without inflating it with an unsourced relief factor or relabeling it as people employed.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Actual headcount, employer/contractor status, simultaneous posts, schedules, relief coverage, leave, occupations, payroll, and worker residence

derivation.formula: 24 hours/day × 365 days/year ÷ (40 hours/week × 52 weeks/year)
assumptions: At least one onsite NOC coverage position was continuously occupied as the operator statement says.
One zero-leave FTE-equivalent supplies 2,080 scheduled hours per year.
No relief factor or multiplier is applied.

limitations: FTE-equivalent coverage is not employee headcount or payroll.
Employment relationship, contractor status, worker residence, occupation, wages, benefits, and actual staffing levels are unknown.
Real operations require breaks, leave, training, overlap, and relief, so actual labor supporting one continuous post would exceed this zero-leave floor.
The 2012 statement does not establish persistence at the same staffing arrangement in later years.
estimates.notes: Conditional mathematical lower bound only. Do not count as observed employees, filled jobs, resident employment, or a current staffing snapshot.
